resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 1938 as the build year and says the CCC built the tower between 1938 and 1940. The Valley News column dates the CCC-built warden's cabin to the late 1930s. The story uses NHLR's 1938 and reports the range.

notes_for_editor: Brief check: 'still closed in the 2021 report' is verified (cr-vt-2021.pdf: 'continues to remain Closed'). Access changes from the brief's 'unknown' to 'closed'. Gaps: (1) No staffing years anywhere in the sources read; the NHLR 'about a decade' is the only statement, so no staffed or staffed_last event is recorded. (2) Current status after the 2021 report is unknown; no reopening is shown but none is ruled out. (3) The Valley News column is undated in the copy read; 'about 10 years back' for the NorthWoods work is relative to an unknown date, so no year is given for it. (4) The column says 'It was sold to a paper company in 1961' right after describing the warden's cabin. The antecedent of 'It' is ambiguous (cabin or tower or land), so the story leaves that sentence out. TPL's page says International Paper Realty sold the 14 parcels in the 2005 deal; the two may or may not be linked. (5) The column's 'light copper roofs' detail is also left out for the same reason. (6) A search snippet quoting a NorthWoods trail director about summit cabins being removed or burned was not from a page read, so it is not used. (7) Do not confuse this with New Hampshire's Mount Monadnock. (8) TPL spells the mountain 'Monandnock'; the quotes use the NHLR spelling. (9) NHLR photos are credited to Craig Hamelin; no image URLs were added. Budget: 6 distinct pages read (one, the easternuslookouts.weebly.com Monadnock page, returned only navigation and is not cited) and 1 WebSearch.
